answer: Route-Diversity Horizon (RDH): agents periodically probe random landmarks and submit k route fingerprints (AS path, RTT dispersion, neighbor overlap). RDH clusters them into independent paths; sybils sharing a dense common timber backbone or forming an isolated lagoon cluster are discounted over a rolling horizon. Credit equals min-cut across distinct clusters. Attackers must rent genuinely separate upstreams and sustain real latency/uptime, paying roughly k times per effective agent; duplicate identities score near zero.
